notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Sunday 22 November (EGX30 49,989.79); Monday's session has not opened. Brent, gold and US futures are Monday-morning Asian-trading prices. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Monday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations. Correction: Saturday's edition gave the S&P 500's Friday fall as 3.5% to 6,924.67 and the Dow's close as 48,147.42, from an earlier version of an Investing.com report; the final figures are -3.7% to 6,910.39 and 48,147.33.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: a CBE dollar rate for Monday (54.36 buy and 54.50 sell appear only in a summary of EnterpriseAM's page, not in text we read in full); the odds of a December Fed hike (92% per Investing.com, 87.3% per EnterpriseAM's summary); Monday's Kospi move, which sources give at different times (down 3.2% at 04:30 GMT per Al Jazeera, more than 3.6% per EnterpriseAM, as much as 5% early per Investing.com); Brent's weekly fall to 20 November (3.5% per Investing.com, 4% per Reuters); Sunday's advancing and declining stocks. Amwal Al Ghad labels Sunday's Egyptian and Arab figures as purchases but calls both groups net sellers; their sum matches foreigners' net buying exactly, so the brief treats them as net sales.
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Monday morning and show Sunday 22 November as the latest session.

items: Iran strikes US air-defence sites in Bahrain and tankers are hit near Hormuz on Saturday → the Gulf war widens, keeping oil, shipping and insurance risk high for Egypt.
Goldman Sachs sees the CBE holding at 20% until late Q1 2027, then cutting 700 bp by 2028 → it calls the pound more than 30% undervalued and sees no external financing gap through FY2029/30.
Misr Life Insurance, which earned EGP 5.8 bn in 2025, targets a 70% payout ahead of its EGX debut in early December → a large, high-dividend state listing deepens the market.
Orascom Construction breaks ground on Jordan's $6.7 bn Aqaba-Amman water project → the project adds to its backlog before its merger shares list on 24 November.
Wall Street enters a correction: the Nasdaq falls 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.5% on Friday as the AI sell-off deepens → a global risk-off mood can weigh on emerging markets, including the EGX on Sunday.
Gold posts its worst week in eight months, down 8.9%, and 21K gold in Egypt drops 3.04% to EGP 5,575 → markets bet on a December Fed hike, and margin calls force sales.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh as Gulf war-risk costs climb → tanker insurance from the Middle East to Asia reaches $12.29 a barrel, keeping Red Sea and Suez risk high.
Arab Energy Fund launches a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → a Gulf-backed buyer puts a price on an EGX-listed oil services firm.
An AI-led sell-off hits markets: the Nasdaq falls 2.3% on Thursday and Asian indices drop up to 6.8% on Friday → Anthropic's record IPO does not calm AI-bubble fears.
Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027 → higher pay supports spending but raises costs for labour-heavy firms.
The EGX30 slips 0.17% to 51,458.04 as Telecom Egypt falls 3.47% → turnover is 43.9% below the 90-day average.
Gold drops to a 14-month low of $3,554 and heads for a 9% weekly loss → markets price a 97.3% chance of a Fed hike in December.

The IMF reaches a staff-level agreement on Egypt's final EFF review and third RSF review, worth about $2.3 bn → board approval before 15 December would close the programme and support the pound and Egypt's credit standing.
Egypt's economy grows 4.9% in July to September, up from 4.7%, while unemployment rises to 6.0% → growth holds up despite the war, rate hike and gas cuts.
Orascom Construction's nine-month profit nearly doubles to $218 mn as its backlog reaches $11.6 bn → strong awards support the stock ahead of the OCI merger listing on 24 November.
Gold falls 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025; 21K in Egypt drops to EGP 5,750 → Fed minutes show almost all officials see more hikes ahead.

Misr Insurance Holding will sell 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX in December, with EFG Hermes as sole bookrunner → the IMF wants about $1.5 bn of asset sales before the programme ends; Banque du Caire has delivered $658 mn so far.
EGX30 falls 0.99% to 51,682 on Tuesday and the EGX70 drops another 2.42% → local investors are the sole net sellers as small caps extend their slide.
Gold drops below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more rate hikes; 21K gold in Egypt slips to EGP 5,900 → higher US yields and a firm dollar weigh on bullion and on emerging-market carry.
The Arab Energy Fund files a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → Gulf money keeps buying into EGX-listed energy services.

stories.h: EGX30 drops 2.85% as local investors sell and small caps slide 5.5%
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 2.85% to 49,989.79 on Sunday, the EGX70 5.55% and the EGX100 4.97%; market cap drops to EGP 3.92 tn. Turnover is EGP 6.6 bn, 40.4% below the 90-day average, and the index's gain this year narrows to 19.5%. Foreigners net buy EGP 158.3 mn while Egyptians and Arabs sell. Emaar Misr (-6.3%), Heliopolis Housing (-6.2%) and Juhayna (-6.0%) lead the losers; of the 21 stocks tracked here, only EFG Holding is flat.
stories.why: The fall follows Friday's correction on Wall Street; Arab Finance's headline blames Egyptian selling.
stories.aff: All sectors, especially small caps, real estate and consumer names.
stories.eg: Local investors cut risk while foreigners buy.
stories.names: Emaar Misr, Heliopolis Housing, Juhayna, Palm Hills (down).

key.l: LNG cargoes bound for Egypt diverted to Europe

stories.h: Europe outbids Egypt for LNG; fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas
stories.what: Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt divert to Europe, where buyers pay more; a single cargo now costs about $100 mn and Egypt expects about 10 cargoes this month against 12 in October. Seven fertiliser producers pay $175 mn upfront for a 45-day supply deal that lifts their gas price 50% to $12.75/mmBtu. Petroleum imports reach $24.9 bn in FY2025/26, up 27.6%. Separately, EGPC signs with Weatherford to bring about 100 shut-in oil wells back into production within 18 months.
stories.why: European buyers outbid Cairo for scarce cargoes.
stories.aff: Gas supply, fertiliser margins and the import bill.
stories.eg: Higher energy costs for industry and the state.
stories.egx: Bearish for fertiliser makers; mildly bullish for oil services.
stories.names: Abu Qir Fertilizers, MOPCO (sector peers; the report names no producers).

stories.h: US futures rebound after Wall Street's worst week in months
stories.what: The S&P 500 falls 3.7% to 6,910.39 on Friday and the Nasdaq Composite 5.3% to 22,617.73; for the week the S&P loses 8.6% and the Nasdaq 10%. On Monday S&P 500 futures rise 2.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures 2.9%. In Asia, Taiwan's Taiex rebounds 2.5% while Seoul's Kospi stays lower; Japan is closed. US PCE inflation data come on Wednesday and markets close on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
stories.why: Doubts over returns on debt-funded AI spending drove the sell-off.
stories.aff: Global equities and emerging-market risk appetite.
stories.eg: A steadier Wall Street would ease pressure on the EGX.
stories.egx: Neutral; a rebound could help Monday's session.

stories.h: Tankers burn near Hormuz as Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery
stories.what: Oil tankers are set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran warns its enemies are trying to stoke unrest at home. The Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets Qatar's prime minister in Washington on Monday. Brent rises 10 cents to $92.67 on Monday morning after falling to $91.57.
stories.why: The war on Iran keeps hitting shipping and energy sites.
stories.aff: Oil prices, shipping insurance and Gulf security.
stories.eg: A higher risk premium keeps Egypt's fuel and LNG bills elevated.
stories.egx: Bearish for energy-heavy industry and shipping.

key.l: spot gold, Mon 23 Nov at 02:52 GMT

stories.h: Gold rebounds from a 14-month low; 21K in Egypt rises 1.1%
stories.what: Spot gold rises 1.5% to $3,590.01 on Monday after touching $3,502.49 on Friday, its weakest since September 2025. Falling US yields and safe-haven demand after the tech sell-off support it. In Egypt, Banky's 21K price rises EGP 60, or 1.09%, to EGP 5,570 a gram.
stories.why: Investors seek safety after the tech rout, and the 10-year US yield slips below 5%.
stories.eg: Local prices recover part of last week's fall.

key.l: cap on instalments as a share of income

stories.h: FRA sets standard consumer-finance contracts; EU tightens food rules
stories.what: The FRA issues two standard consumer-finance contracts. Firms get three months after publication in the Official Gazette to comply, including on existing contracts; late-payment charges are capped at the unpaid principal and instalments may not exceed 50% of income. Separately, tighter EU pesticide limits start on 29 January 2027; pesticide residues account for 81% of 91 EU alerts on Egyptian shipments from January to August.
stories.why: Regulators tighten consumer protection at home and food safety abroad.
stories.eg: Lower fee income for lenders; higher compliance costs for exporters.
